Subject: Starlight AI — perf qualification + next steps

Hi Sam — thanks for the time earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our perf/discovery call:

What we heard (SLO targets you care about)
- 95th percentile latency target: ideally <= 120 ms, acceptable up to 180 ms during peak windows
- Steady-state throughput: ~50 RPS, peak bursts up to 150 RPS for short durations
- Concurrency: target ~25 concurrent in-flight requests
- Streaming: token-by-token partial delivery is important; first-byte latency goal for streaming responses ~<=50 ms
- Typical prompts: ~200–250 tokens in, ~60–100 tokens out (avg 80)

Initial qualification plan (what Redwood will run)
- Perf run against a 10k-sample prompt set you provide; we'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tail-kv cache hit rates, and token-level cost estimates
- Test matrix: rw-13b-low-latency (primary) and rw-7b-high-thru (fallback) across quantization profiles (FP16, Q8)
- Load pattern: sustained 50 RPS ramping to 150 RPS bursts, concurrency sweep to 30

Cost / performance levers we'll exercise
- Continuous batching with latency-aware deadlines to reduce per-token cost without blowing p95
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts to lower compute and p95 for warm traffic
- Quantization profiles (8-bit weights) to reduce GPU memory and increase throughput with small quality checks
- Model variants and routing: prefer low-latency 13B for critical paths, route to 7B variant for cost-sensitive fallbacks

Immediate asks for you
1) Share the 10k sample prompts + a handful of golden responses (drop in the Drive link or zip reply)
2) Confirm whether you prefer a hosted trial or Dedicated capacity for the baseline runs (cost tradeoffs attached in the perf plan)
3) Confirm Wed Feb 11 10:00am PT for a 30-min follow-up where we’ll review initial test config

Attachments: starlight_perf_plan_v1.pdf (attached), latency_sample_traces.zip (referenced)

If that aligns, we’ll spin up a scoped trial API key and schedule the perf runs.

Thanks — look forward to progressing.

—

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before the follow-up:

- On the 95th <= 120 ms: is that something you can expect to hit on the rw-13b-low-latency variant without dedicated capacity, or will that require Reserved/Dedicated?
- For streaming requirements, our UX team needs ordering guarantees for partial tokens (we can tolerate reordering within 30ms window but want monotonic append). Can your runtime provide that consistently?
- Security/compliance: we need SOC2 evidence and a quick note on KMS/HSM support for key material during the trial

Attaching a small trace (starlight_trace_20260209.har) that represents a 2-minute burst profile we observed in prod. Also dropped the 1k sample prompts in the Drive link you shared.

We can confirm Wed 2/11 10am PT. If you can outline in the meeting whether the 120ms p95 is feasible without Dedicated, that’ll help budget discussions.

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:05:14 -0800
Subject: Internal: starlight perf test config proposal

Quick internal note to capture the config we should run for tomorrow's call and the perf run we promised:

Recommended baseline test config:
- Model variants: rw-13b-q8-latency (primary), rw-7b-q4-highthru (fallback routing)
- Quantization: q8_0 for main run; run FP16 toggles for quality comparison (sample golden set of 200 prompts)
- Continuous batching: enabled, soft window 20–30ms, max batch size 64, latency-aware scheduling to honor p95 SLO
- KV cache: enabled for prefix-heavy prompts, TTL 2 hours, pre-warm with a 1k hot-set
- Load generator: sustained 60 RPS for 20 min, 3x burst windows to 150 RPS for 60s every 5 min, concurrency sweep 5 -> 30
- Streaming mode: chunked streaming with first-token deadline 30–50ms (aim for <=50ms TTFB) and ordered assembly on client side

Telemetry and outputs to collect:
- p50/p95/p99 per endpoint, per-variant and per-quant profile
- GPU utilization and kernel breakdown (compilation/kernel selection logs)
- Effective tokens per-second and token cost estimate per variant
- Cache hit ratio and latency delta for warm vs cold

Notes / ops asks:
- Need the full 10k prompt corpus and the 200 golden responses for quality checks before we toggle q8
- Confirm whether they want test to run on Hosted API or request a dedicated 2-week trial (Monica: we should recommend dedicated trial for representative tail behavior)

I’ll prepare the perf job spec and attach the load-gen script and config.

—Monica

Sam — great call yesterday. Finalizing next steps and what we'll deliver during the scoped trial:

What we will run
1) Two-week dedicated trial (recommended) with the rw-13b-q8-latency variant as the primary profile and rw-7b-q4 as fallback routing.
2) Perf matrix: sustained 50–60 RPS, burst to 150 RPS, concurrency ramps to 30. We’ll run the 10k prompt set and the 200 golden responses for quality regression checks.

Levers we will exercise to pursue p95 <= 120ms
- Continuous batching: aggressive latency-aware batching with 20–30ms soft window to increase throughput while bound p95
- Prefix/KV caching: pre-warm hot prompts to reduce compute on repeated queries and improve warm p95
- Quantization profile: q8 (8-bit) weights for primary run (profiled against FP16 on the golden set)
- Model routing: primary low-latency 13B; automated fallback to 7B variant when queueing would violate SLOs or to reduce cost for non-critical traffic

Security/compliance and logistics
- SOC2: we will provide the SOC2 snapshot and our SOC2 artifact page during the onboarding ticket
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration for Private/Dedicated deployments; for hosted trial we can use scoped encryption and sign appropriate agreements

Deliverables and timeline
- Perf run artifacts (p50/p95/p99, GPU/kernels, cache hit rates, token cost models) — delivered 3 business days after test completion
- Draft SOW for a paid Dedicated pilot (attached: SOW-starlight-draft.docx)
- Proposed follow-up: Wed Feb 18 10am PT to review results and next steps

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/7842), Perf plan (attached), Drive perf folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PerfPlaybook

If you confirm the dedicated trial, I’ll spin up the environment and send a scoped API key + run schedule.
